name: Sanctions & coercion
value: EU weighs Iran sanctions; FMs meet 16 Nov
summary: EU set to discuss new Iran sanctions on 16 Nov after France blamed an IRGC cyber unit for supermarket attacks
state: On 10 Nov France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's Revolutionary Guards carried out the October cyberattacks on refrigeration at about 700 supermarket sites and that the EU would impose sanctions on those responsible (SBS News). EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on 9 Nov the response must be firm, and foreign ministers are due to discuss it on 16 Nov (Demócrata). Searches on 14 Nov found no major economy cut off from payment systems and no large sovereign-asset seizure.
for_you: New sanctions mainly affect firms trading with or financing the targeted entities. Businesses with exposure to Iran-linked trade face compliance checks; UK rules are published by OFSI.
rubric_hit: Watch: major new EU package on Iran under preparation; no payment-system cut-off or sovereign seizure

sources.title: SBS News — France blames Iran for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges
Demócrata — Kallas proposes new sanctions against Iran for cyberattacks on European supermarkets

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.
